summary.text: Saint Pulcheria was a Byzantine empress who supported Orthodox teaching, church building, and the councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon.

blocks.text: She was a daughter of Emperor Arcadius and sister of Theodosius II. The OCA describes her as her brother’s coregent and adviser, with a broad education and an active commitment to Orthodox teaching.
blocks.locator: Opening paragraph on Arcadius, TheodosiusIIand education

blocks.text: Court conflict temporarily removed her from power. After returning, and after her brother’s death, she married the new emperor Marcian. The received life says that the marriage preserved her chosen virginity. She also supported churches and monasteries.

blocks.text: The life records her giving wealth to the poor and the Church. She died peacefully in 453 at the age of 54. It does not describe martyrdom.

blocks.text: Her legacy in the cited source concerns patronage and defense of Orthodox doctrine, particularly around Ephesus in 431 and Chalcedon in 451. These were episcopal councils; her support did not turn the empress herself into a bishop or the author of their definitions.
